Alibaba is a company out of China. Its market cap is about 250 billion, making it roughly the size of Toyota. A division of that company called Alibaba Cloud is responsible for making the Qwen models. The US government has accused Alibaba of distilling models proprietary models from the US to create this model. It's hard to have a problem with that when companies like Anthropic and OpenAI have stolen the corpus of all human produced text and video to train their models. 

As far as the Qwen models, they are some of the best models you can run on limited hardware. For example, Qwen 3.8 27B takes up just 56 gigabytes of room in memory, making it a game changer for local LLM setups on a budget.

Deepseek is another company out of China that started just in twenty twenty-three. It's a medium sized company with under four hundred employees and a private valuation of around $74 billion. 

Deepseek produced one of my favorite models of all time. Deepseek V 4.1 flash. This was the model that really caught everyone's attention because people started running it locally and were getting results comparable to Opus 5.5. 

It should be exciting to see what Deepseek does in the future.

This is a solid harness From Deep Seek. It's tuned to be most useful with Deep Seek models, but it serves as a great source of information for Neuman as Deep Seek tends to innovate and share their progress.

Pi is one of my favorite harnesses. I used it extensively before building Neuman and partially to build Neuman. What I love about Pi is its simplicity. A lot of these harnesses become a mass of code produced by swarms of agents running 24/7, and they become completely incomprehensible and often very buggy. Pi took a very different approach in being a very minimal harness that you can customize. I think it's a great project and it serves as a invaluable source of information for guiding Neuman's harness.

The DGX Spark is an interesting machine from Nvidia. It reminds me of the Mac Studio in its footprint and its power. You can also combine up to eight of these to run massive models with a whopping 1024GB of memory.

The DGX Sparks is a great machine for a research lab or a small team. With 748GB of memory, it's an extremely powerful machine. The footprint is not too big either and looks like a large desktop computer.
